Polyethylene Oxide Polietileno, óxido de. Pharmacopoeias. In USNF. USNF 26 (Polyethylene Oxide). A nonionic homopolymer of ethylene oxide, represented by the formula (OCH2CH2)n, in which n represents the average number of oxyethylene groups (about 2000 to over 100 000). It is obtainable in several grades, varying in viscosity profile in an aqueous isopropyl alcohol solu- tion. It may contain not more than 3% of silicon dioxide. A white to off-white powder. Miscible with water; freely soluble in ace- tonitrile, in dichloromethane, in ethylene dichloride, and in trichloroethylene; insoluble in aliphatic hydrocarbons, in ethyl- ene glycol, in diethylene glycol, and in glycerol. Store in airtight containers. Protect from light. Uses Polyethylene oxide is used as a tablet binder and as a suspending and thickening agent in pharmaceutical preparations. Polyethyl- ene oxide has been used in hydrogel wound dressings.
